title: Define beta scope + success criteria for SIEM-ready audit export
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Initiative: lock beta definition for SIEM-ready audit export so Engineering can build to a stable scope and SRE/Security can set launch criteria.

Context
- Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation project.
- Customer problem: audit events exist but aren’t easily exported to SIEM/log pipelines with reliable delivery, consistent schema, and operational visibility.

Beta goals (what “good” looks like)
1) Deliver audit events to customer-owned destinations with production-grade reliability semantics:
   - Delivery: at-least-once
   - Buffering: durable queue + retry/backoff + DLQ
   - Explicit destination health states (OK/Degraded/Paused/Failed) surfaced in Console
   - Dedupe guidance and stable event identifiers
2) Reduce SIEM cost/noise with filtering (customer-controlled, validated).
3) Publish a stable, versioned audit event schema suitable for SIEM correlation.
4) Make the feature operable: metrics/dashboards, SLOs/alerts, runbooks, replay tooling.

Beta scope (MVP)
Destinations (initial sinks)
- Splunk HEC (primary)
- Datadog Logs intake
- S3 (hourly partitioning, compressed objects, encryption options)

Configuration surface
- Console UX behind a per-tenant feature flag:
  - Create destination (type + endpoint/bucket + credentials)
  - Configure filters
  - “Send test event” / verify connectivity
  - Destination detail view: last delivered time, last error, backlog estimate, status
- API endpoints for destination CRUD + health/status fields for Console.

Filtering requirements
- Support include/exclude semantics at minimum:
  - event_type
  - actor (user/service)
  - workspace/tenant
  - environment (prod/staging where applicable)
  - time window (for replay tooling; not for continuous filtering)
  - optionally: IP/region (if present in event)
- Validation:
  - deny unsafe filters that would drop all events without explicit confirmation
  - field allowlist (no arbitrary JSONPath queries)
  - sane defaults: if no filters set, export all audit events included in schema v1

Delivery semantics (beta contract)
- At-least-once: duplicates possible under retry/replay.
- Ordering: best-effort; not guaranteed globally across destinations.
- Replay:
  - Operator/customer-initiated replay of a bounded time window
  - Requires explicit confirmation and generates an audit event (“audit.export.replay_requested”)

Out of scope (explicit non-goals for beta)
- Exactly-once delivery.
- Support for >3 sinks (no generic webhook, no Kafka, no Azure Event Hub, etc.).
- Custom per-customer field mappings beyond schema v1.
- Full historical backfill for all tenants (beta supports forward-only export + bounded replay tooling; any “backfill” is best-effort per destination with safeguards).
- Full UI for advanced routing/multi-destination fanout policies beyond basic multiple destinations per tenant.

Beta gating + enablement plan
- Gated by per-tenant feature flag with allowlist/denylist support.
- Beta access criteria (minimum):
  - Enterprise contract / security-reviewed customers
  - Identified SIEM owner + on-call escalation contact
  - Agreement to weekly feedback + share sample dashboards/queries
- Rollout phases:
  1) Internal dogfood (Redwood’s own Splunk)
  2) 2 design partners (one Splunk, one Datadog)
  3) Expand to 3–5 total beta customers
- Rollback conditions:
  - Sustained delivery failure rate above threshold (see Success Metrics)
  - Backlog unbounded growth / worker retry storm
  - Credential leakage risk / P0 security incident

Target launch window
- Beta start: 2025-04-15 (feature-flagged)
- Beta hardening checkpoint: 2025-05-06
- Beta expansion: 2025-05-20

Success metrics (beta)
Product metrics
- Setup success: 80%+ of beta tenants complete destination setup + receive test event within 1 business day of onboarding.
- Adoption: 3–5 active beta tenants exporting continuously for >= 14 days.
- Filtering usefulness: >= 2 beta tenants use filters and report measurable noise reduction (qualitative + token/ingest volume estimate).

Reliability / SLO-style metrics (beta acceptance thresholds)
- End-to-end delivery latency (p95): <= 120s for Hosted (measured from event emitted to acknowledged by sink / object committed).
- Delivery success rate: >= 99.5% over 7 days per destination (excluding customer-caused auth failures; those must be visible and actionable).
- Backlog bound: backlog drains to steady-state within 30 minutes after peak load periods for Hosted.
- DLQ: DLQ volume <= 0.01% of events; any DLQ growth triggers alerting and runbook action.

Security/compliance acceptance criteria
- Credentials encrypted at rest; access scoped to audit-export service.
- RBAC: only Workspace Admin (or equivalent) can create/update/delete destinations.
- Auditability: export config changes generate audit events (who/what/when).
- Data handling: schema v1 PII classification + redaction rules published; exporter must not add new PII.

Required artifacts / deliverables (beta readiness)
- PRD + design spec + ADRs finalized (delivery semantics, Splunk auth/ack, S3 partitioning/encryption).
- Audit Event Schema v1 published with examples + backward compatibility rules.
- Customer docs:
  - Splunk HEC setup guide
  - Datadog logs intake setup guide
  - S3 sink setup + IAM/KMS guidance
  - Dedupe guidance + known limitations
- Operability:
  - Dashboards + alerts
  - Runbooks (backlog drain/replay, credential rotation, connector failures)
  - On-call ownership + escalation paths

comments: 2025-01-24 (Priya Natarajan): Agree on at-least-once for beta; need very clear customer messaging on duplicates + replay behavior. Please ensure we define an explicit dedupe key in schema v1 and carry it through to all sinks.

2025-01-27 (Sean Gallagher): For gating, I want a hard requirement that we have at least one internal dogfood tenant running for 7 days before onboarding external beta customers. Also please include rollback conditions tied to backlog growth and connector retry storms.

2025-01-29 (Marcus Lin): Scope looks good. Need explicit mention that export destination config changes must themselves be audited (create/update/delete/test/replay). Also require credential encryption at rest + least privilege access path.

2025-02-03 (Chloe Martin): Console flow needs a minimal but clear “health widget” (last delivered, last error, status). Please keep filters limited for beta; we can iterate after we validate performance impact and validation UX.

2025-02-05 (Olga Petrov): Add note that schema v1 must include PII classification/redaction guidance and that export does not increase data retention obligations on Redwood’s side beyond existing audit log retention policy.

2025-03-18 (Naomi Feldman): Marking Done after incorporating Security/SRE/GRC requirements, confirming beta launch window, and aligning success metrics with Platform/SRE. Next: drive PM-4823/4824/4825 to completion and support ENG-13920 rollout checklist.
